response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS n FROM film f JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg_n FROM r) SELECT SUM(r.n) AS total_films_in_stock, AVG(r.n - a.avg_n) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM r CROSS JOIN a WHERE r.n > a.avg_n

assumptions.assumption: 'Films in inventory' means distinct films that have at least one inventory copy, counted per rating. A film with several copies counts once.
The across-rating average is the unweighted mean of the five per-rating counts, so ratings with no stocked films are not included.

alternatives.interpretation: 'Films in inventory' means physical copies (inventory rows) per rating, so a film with several copies counts several times.
alternatives.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS n FROM film f JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg_n FROM r) SELECT SUM(r.n) AS total_films_in_stock, AVG(r.n - a.avg_n) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM r CROSS JOIN a WHERE r.n > a.avg_n
